newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan cautious on using tax money for bad loans.
newsitem.headline: Japan cautious on using tax money for bad loans.

text.p: Japanese authorities will tackle the problem of bad loans held by financial institutions taking into account the conditions at the time, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a parliamentary committee on Tuesday.
Asked whether the government had any plans to use fresh public funds to deal with the bad loan issue, Mitsuzuka said the government's stance on the issue was unchanged.

He said he will stick to the previous stance that the government should not get involved in the resolution of bad loans held at non-bank financial institutions other than those at the failed "jusen" mortgage firms.
But he added: "We will tackle the bad loan issue taking into account the conditions at the time with an aim of protecting depositors and ensuring the stability of the financial system."
The government last year budgeted 685 billion yen in tax money to help wind up failed mortgage firms.

The issue of pitching in tax money has recently come into the spotlight again after an opposition politician made a call to reopen debate on the issue, followed by supportive comments by key members of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party.
